data.name: Warren
data.gender_notes: Warren is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Warren originated from the Old English words war, which means 'red', and wearn, meaning 'protector'. It was a common name for warriors in Anglo-Saxon England. The name also has associations with the red color of battle and the protective role of warriors in society. The name Warren carries the meaning “Red protector” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Warren usually hope their child will grow to embody red protector and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Warren belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Red protector.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Warren total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

It became a common surname among families of noble or military heritage. Today, the name is recognized and used worldwide, reflecting the global influence of English language and culture.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Warren can be seen as a reminder of God's protection and provision in times of conflict and danger. The red color associated with the name is reminiscent of the blood of Christ, shed for the forgiveness of sins and the salvation of humanity. Thus, the name Warren can inspire faith, courage, and a sense of God's presence in the midst of challenges and battles.

It also signifies one's role as a spiritual warrior, ever vigilant and prepared to battle against the forces of darkness.
